title: Metering Service Training Q&A: How Far Back a Referee Backbill Settlement Reaches
content:
For a **Metering Service** referee backbill settlement, the billing months the settlement reaches back follow what the meter's own records show about when the under-registration began. The records read are the meter's installation record (its installation reason and date), the meter's test results, and the effective date of the current rate schedule on the Electric Service Agreement.

## The rule

Where the meter was set by a failed-meter replacement or a test exchange and has no within-tolerance test result on record, the error is dated from the installation and the billing months the referee backbill settlement reaches back are all the whole calendar months between the installation date and the company test date.

Where the meter has a within-tolerance test result on record and the service agreement's current rate schedule took effect after the latest such result, the billing months the referee backbill settlement reaches back are the whole calendar months between the schedule's effective date and the company test date.

In every other case neither of these datings applies.

## Questions the rule answers

**The meter went in as a failed-meter replacement and has never tested within tolerance. Where does the reach-back start?** At the installation date: every whole calendar month from installation to the company test date is reached back.

**The meter tested within tolerance once and the agreement later moved to a new schedule. Where does it start?** At the date the current schedule took effect, provided that date is after the latest within-tolerance result.

**The meter was set by a test exchange but did test within tolerance later.** The installation dating does not apply, because a within-tolerance result is on record; the schedule dating applies only if the current schedule took effect after that result.

**The schedule took effect on the same day as the latest within-tolerance result.** It did not take effect after it, so the schedule dating does not apply.

## Hypothetical illustration

A meter set on 14 August 2023 by a failed-meter replacement, never tested within tolerance, with a company test on 30 June 2025: the whole calendar months from 14 August 2023 to 30 June 2025 are 22, and all 22 are reached back.
